column1: ## The window thread's waits: the one registry (design note 2026-09-26; budget note R7).
## Six sections, each a header line then tab-separated lines. A line starting `##` is a comment.
## Some seven-cell `worker-door-body` effect rows therefore end in a tab; `.gitattributes`
## exempts this registry from blank-at-EOL diagnostics because the parser counts that empty cell.
## `# rows` — ARCHITECTURE §5.3, one line per numbered exception. `status` is `done` (repaid:
## what remains on the window thread is its residue, still listed), `open` (to be moved),
## `ruled to stay`, or `pending` (found and recorded, not ruled). The §5.3 table is generated from
## this section by `scripts/dev/generate-window-waits-table.ps1`; edit here, never there.
## `# doors` — one line per `bt_platform::admission::doors` type, in its order: the §5.3 row it
## serves, the `hang_watch::Station` its meter enters, the phases it is admitted in, the call it
## admits, where the admission is minted, and what one admission measures. Held equal to the
## types by `hang_watch::window_waits_tests`. Every door takes its token, minted where the line says (A1d).
## `# vocabulary` — the effects that wait (or are counted beside the waits), with the targets
## they exist on (`all`, `windows`, `macos`; every entry names at least one). A2 compares it with
## the lint's list. It lists library paths and cross-crate entrances a caller outside the crate can
## name: a private function is not an entry, and its raw effects are sites of their own
## `# entrances` — the cross-crate entrances that left the vocabulary because their signature is
## the door (revision (j)5): each takes, on every `cfg` arm it is written on, a parameter whose
## type is exactly `WaitToken<'_, doors::<door>>` for the door named here — never an `Option` of
## one — so no call of it compiles without an admission. The guard checks each, per arm, and
## refuses one that is also in `# vocabulary`.
## `# effects` — one line per **effect function**: the function whose own body holds a listed effect,
## keyed by crate, `cfg` arm and item, with its entries and their counts, its kind (`owner-door-body`,
## `WorkerCtx`, `none (transport)`, `drop`) and the door it serves (revision (j)7). A2e puts one
## `expect` on each. Today it holds exactly the effect functions already inside a registered door;
## revision (k) allocates the rest. Held equal to the bodies by
## A `worker-door-body` row (revision (j)13, brought forward by U-28) is a worker's door: its function takes
## a `WorkerCtx`, and its door column is empty, because the admission identities are the window thread's.
## `# doors` (admission identities) and `# owners` (FFI constructs) stay separate lists: neither is a
## list of `expect` holders, and no `# owners` module is exempt from the bare-site inventory.
## A `worker-door-body` row's last field (door) is empty, and the row still ends in its tab: every
## line of a section has exactly its header's seven cells. `.gitattributes` exempts this file from
## `git diff --check`'s blank-at-eol rule for that reason alone.
## `# owners` — where the constructs a lint cannot see through may be written (budget note §C-3):
## and `#[macro_export]`, each by owner — the product item it is written in, or the module when it
## is written in none (inside `define_class!`) — with its count. A construct or owner not listed
## here is refused, and so is a listed one that is gone; counts taken from the code (A1e).
## Windows's undocumented `MessageBoxTimeoutW` has no `windows` 0.62.2 binding, so
## `windows_impl::message_box` owns its one narrow declaration and link attribute.

column5: **open — narrowed by ticket 54**: the environment is asked for once on an idle turn after startup (`Runtime::warm_web_engine`, station `warm_web_engine`), which takes its 8.5–39 ms out of the first page's gesture; the environment starts no runtime process (measured), so the controller and the pump dispatch are still the first page's, and a new ruling is owed for them (D-64). **Narrowed again by ticket 60 (ruled 2026-09-25, option A):** for a profile that has opened a page (`web_pages_used`), the controller call (≤ 590 ms worst on the clean VM) moves to a quiet idle turn under `make_spare_web_controller`, and the first eligible page's window-thread cost is the rehost walk (`adopt_spare_web_controller`, 11–73 ms on the VM) and a navigate — 2318 → 146 ms median to the first page in spike 59. Still the first page's: a profile's first-ever page, a page that arrives before the spare has landed, and every page after the spare is used (~0.6 s warm, ~2.3 s cold); open for 0.4.6. Not movable to a lane: WebView2 refuses an environment used from any thread but the one that created it (`0x802A000C`, measured), so the environment, the controller and the engine's callbacks all belong to the window thread with the controller (§5.2); the pump after the first page is named per message since ticket 64

column5: **ruled to stay** (`DESIGN.md`, 2026-09-28, *every road process of an update leaves through one exit guard*): the loop has returned and every window is gone; the process must not end before the start that replaces it is delivered, and the wait is bounded; during it no window of this process exists, so the person sees Folio gone until the applier's trial or the replacement appears, and the message box appears when nothing was delivered: at the latest at the bound, earlier when every start has already failed. The box itself is shown on this thread after the wait (`bt_platform::standalone_alert`, U-32) and is synchronous: the process returns when it is answered or at the latest after `STANDALONE_ALERT_WITHIN` (15 min), when macOS takes its system alert away or Windows's ownerless `MessageBoxTimeoutW` returns
